title: Why Do Dogs Sniff Everything On Walks?
description:
Their nose reads the world like a newspaper.

script: If your dog stops every ten feet to sniff a patch of grass, they're not stalling, they're reading. A dog's nose has up to three hundred million scent receptors compared to our six million, and a huge part of their brain is dedicated to processing smell. Every sniff tells them who else walked by, what mood that dog was in, whether a squirrel passed through recently, even how long ago. It's basically a full news feed of the neighborhood. That's why letting your dog actually sniff on walks matters so much for their mental stimulation, it's not just exercise for their legs, it's a full workout for their brain. So next time they stop and sniff for what feels like forever, just let them read the paper.
